name: Maserati 4CLT/48
description:
4CLT/48 "San Remo": 4 cyl in-line, 78 * 78mm = 1491cc, 4 valves/cyl, twin overhead camshafts, two-stage Roots supercharger, 260 bhp @ 7000 rpm

Design: Ernesto Maserati / Alberto Massimino
Transmission: 4 speed gearbox
Chassis: Tubular ladder frame
Suspension: Front: double wishbones, coil springs, hydraulic dampers Rear: quarter-elliptic leaf springs, hydraulic dampers
Dimensions: Wheelbase: 2500mm, dry weight: 620 kg
Top speed: 270 km/h
Years: 1948-1950

The 4CL rebuilt around a tubular frame and a two-stage blower, and the car that made the privateer respectable again. Ascari and Villoresi won first time out at San Remo in 1948 and the name stuck to the model. In 1949 the Automovil Club Argentino bought two for Juan Manuel Fangio, who took the second of them to San Remo and won that race as well, on his first European start of the season.
author: Legion
